relevance.rationale: Directly on the corpus's central algebra, but one step to the side of where the compute lives. QOU works with the finite Iwahori-Hecke algebras H_n(q) and their Markov trace; Solleveld works with AFFINE Hecke algebras H(R,q) with possibly unequal parameters. The corpus does have a named affine open item — folio/quantum-observable-universe/braids-and-knots/markov-trace-inductive-limit.lean states 'The full operator-theoretic construction (von Neumann inductive limit on the infinite-dim affine Hecke algebra) is the open R&D content' — and Solleveld's Theorem 2 is exactly a structural computation of the homology (hence the trace-functional data) of that algebra, with the striking conclusion that it does not depend on q at all. Held to supporting rather than core because nothing in the current compute path consumes it: QOU's Markov trace is built at finite n from Hoefsmit/Wedderburn data, and the inductive limit is scaffolding, not a live consumer. Honest caveat to carry into any citation: the v3 abstract itself records a 2021 CORRECTION — 'some problems with the construction of families of representations surfaced, these are discussed on pages 16, 18, 19 and 22' — so Theorem 1 must not be cited as unqualified.

keyResults.statement: For epsilon in C outside sqrt(-1)R^*, HH_*(H(R,q^epsilon)) is isomorphic to the W-invariant algebraic differential forms Omega^*(T~)^W on the extended quotient of the torus by the Weyl group — in particular independent of the parameter q.
keyResults.useForFolio: A q-independence statement for the homological invariants of the affine Hecke algebra, which is the structural backdrop for the inductive-limit trace object the corpus leaves open. It says the trace-theoretic data of the algebra is rigid in q, so any q-dependence QOU observes in a Markov-trace-derived quantity must come from the REPRESENTATION/evaluation side, not from the homology of the algebra — a useful, checkable separation of concerns for the fibre-vs-archimedean distinction AGENTS.md insists on.

keyResults.statement: For epsilon outside sqrt(-1)R^*, two representations pi(w,i,t,epsilon) and pi(w',i',t',epsilon) have the SAME TRACE iff w = w', i = i' and t, t' lie in one Z_W(w)-orbit; and the collection forms a Q-basis of the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional H(R,q^epsilon)-representations.
keyResults.useForFolio: A trace-separation criterion: it says precisely which representation data a trace functional can and cannot distinguish. That is the affine analogue of the question QOU's Markov trace answers at finite n (traces separate Wedderburn blocks indexed by partitions), and it is the statement the inductive-limit construction would need in order to know its limiting trace is faithful. Cite with the v3 correction caveat attached.

keyResults.statement: The representations of the family H(R,q^epsilon), epsilon in C, come in families depending analytically on epsilon (matrix coefficients conjecturally algebraic in q^{1/2}).
keyResults.useForFolio: An analyticity-in-the-deformation-parameter statement for Hecke representations. This is the affine instance of the fibre-level framing AGENTS.md sets out for c_k(q) — the object is analytic in q at the fibre level, and each substrate anchor is one evaluation of it. It supports that framing with an external theorem rather than an assertion, though it does not establish it for the finite H_n(q) the corpus computes with.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan: no Solleveld entry exists, and this is the standard reference for the homology of the exact algebra the corpus's inductive-limit item names. Suggested id solleveld2022hochschild. The ref note must record the 2021 correction on pp. 16, 18, 19, 22.

The inductive-limit Lean file declares the affine construction 'open R&D content' with no literature pointer. A remark recording what IS known about the affine algebra's trace/homology data — Theorem 2's q-independence and Theorem 1(d)'s trace-separation criterion, with the correction caveat — turns an unscoped open item into one with a stated starting point, without wiring anything.
